name: logic_gate_simulator
spec: Create a graphical logic gate simulator in Python using Pygame. The simulator provides an infinite scrollable and zoomable canvas where users can place logic gates, connect them with wires, and simulate digital circuits in real time. The simulator must support saving and loading circuits in a defined JSON format, detect combinational cycles, and include a clock generator and seven segment display component.
features: A pygame window opens showing an infinite canvas with a dot-grid background
Canvas can be panned by clicking and dragging with the middle mouse button or holding space and left dragging
Canvas can be zoomed in and out with the scroll wheel maintaining zoom centered on the cursor position
A toolbar shows available components: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR gates
Additional components available in the toolbar: INPUT node, OUTPUT node, CLOCK generator, SEVEN SEGMENT DISPLAY
Left clicking a component in the toolbar enters placement mode and left clicking the canvas places that component
Placed components can be selected by left clicking them
Selected components can be dragged to new positions by clicking and dragging
Multiple components can be selected with a rubber band drag selection box
Selected components can be deleted with the Delete key
Components have clearly visible labeled input and output pins rendered as small circles on their edges
Wires are drawn by clicking an output pin then clicking an input pin and snap to the grid
Wires route orthogonally with automatic corner handling
A wire can be deleted by right clicking it
Each input pin accepts only one wire connection while output pins can connect to multiple inputs
The simulation runs continuously updating all gate outputs based on current inputs every frame
INPUT nodes can be toggled between HIGH and LOW by clicking them
OUTPUT nodes display their current HIGH or LOW state with distinct colors and a label
CLOCK generator component automatically oscillates between HIGH and LOW at a configurable frequency shown in Hz
SEVEN SEGMENT DISPLAY component accepts 7 input wires and renders the corresponding digit segment pattern visually
Cycle detection identifies combinational loops and highlights the involved wires and components in red with a warning message
Signal propagation correctly handles arbitrary depth of connected gates in the correct topological order
Components display their current output state color visually during simulation using green for HIGH and grey for LOW
Pressing Ctrl+S saves the current circuit to a JSON file prompting for a filename
Pressing Ctrl+O opens a prompt to enter a filename and loads a circuit from that JSON file
The JSON circuit format stores component types, positions, unique IDs, configuration, and wire connections between specific pin IDs
A sample circuit file is included demonstrating a half adder built from basic gates
A sample circuit file is included demonstrating a 4-bit ripple counter using clock and gate combinations
Right clicking a component opens a small properties panel to rename it or configure its clock frequency
The canvas shows a coordinate display and zoom level percentage indicator as a corner overlay
